intro.title: After Closing
intro.narrator: Some days smell of tiredness, pepper, and the things you never had time to say.
intro.text:
You finally close the shop.

The neon sign above the window flickers one last time.

*Horlogerie Verneuil — Repairs & Restorations*

You put your tools back into their velvet case.
The tiny pliers.
The loupes.
The springs, fine as hair.

Outside, the city runs.
It always runs.

You spend the evening fixing watches nobody looks at anymore.

Sometimes you wonder whether time still exists at all.
Or whether people are just pretending.

You eat a reheated blanquette standing in the kitchen.

It's good, all the same.

You fall asleep on the couch.

choices.text: Step into the dream

hub_start.title: The Workbench of Dreams
hub_start.narrator: In dreams, even counters can drift away.
hub_start.text:
You open your eyes behind your workbench.

But the shop is not quite the same anymore.

The watches on the shelves run backward.
The hands spin around the dial in a few seconds.
Or in several hours. Hard to say.

A ladle appears on the workbench, shining like a precision tool.

Three doors take shape in the back wall.

The city rumbles behind each of them.

choices.text: Go through the clock door with your bag
Watch the dream cat

chat_hub.title: The Cat on the Counter
chat_hub.narrator: Some guides prefer to sleep on the answers.
chat_hub.text:
The cat is lying on the workbench.

It opens one eye as you approach.

Around it lie dismantled watches whose gears keep turning all by themselves.

**"You repair time."**

It doesn't really speak.
But you understand all the same.

**"Then you should know this one is broken."**

choices.text: Stroke it before you leave
Ask it to show you the way

ville_intro.title: The City That Runs
ville_intro.text:
You arrive in a city where everyone is running.

People eat while they walk.
Children do their homework on the subway.
People check their watches, but they don't read the time — they just watch the hands move.

As if checking were enough.
As if time passed better when you kept an eye on it.

You take out your repairer's loupe.

Every watch you can see is set to the same time.

Not the right one.

choices.text: Go talk to the old lady
Follow the stressed student
Enter the subway without stopping
Try the express restaurant
You catch a delicious smell drifting out of your bag: you can set up a table and serve the blanquette

vieille_dame.title: The Woman on the Bench
vieille_dame.narrator: Sometimes, someone wants less an answer than a presence.
vieille_dame.text:
You sit down beside her.

She doesn't seem surprised.

**"Everyone walks past at a run."**

You ask her since when.

**"Since we decided that wasted time was a fault."**

She takes an old watch from her pocket.
The dial is cracked.
The hands have stopped.

**"My husband wore it. He never ran."**

She slips the watch back into her pocket.

**"It stopped the day he stopped running too."**

choices.text: Invite the passersby to sit down
Ask why nobody stays

rue_sans_pause.title: The Street Without a Pause
rue_sans_pause.narrator: A city that never pauses eventually forgets why it moves forward.
rue_sans_pause.text:
You watch the passersby.

They are all running in the same direction.

But at the end of the street, there is a wall.

They turn right.
Run on.
Turn left.
Run on.

A loop.

You look at their wrists.
Each watch shows a different time.
But all of them are running too fast.

*Someone has wound every spring too tight.*

You know this problem.

choices.text: Set the big table up in the middle of the avenue
Ignore the cat and run

etudiant_presse.title: The Stressed Student
etudiant_presse.narrator: Success sometimes takes the form of a pile of papers blowing away.
etudiant_presse.text:
The student gathers his papers with trembling hands.

**"I'm late."**

A sheet flies off.
It bears an exam date.

But the date is tomorrow.

**"You're not late."**

He looks at you as if you were speaking a foreign language.

**"If I don't run, I'm late."**

He runs off again.

You check your watch.
Yours is keeping the right pace.

That's why it looks broken to everyone else.

choices.text: Offer him a plate
Run with him

metro.title: The Subway That Never Stops
metro.narrator: Some trains lead nowhere, yet everyone boards them anyway.
metro.text:
The subway has been running for a very long time.

People stare at the floor.

A man sleeps standing up, a briefcase clutched to his chest.
A woman answers messages with a faraway look.
A teenager listens to music with his eyes closed — he's the only one who seems to be breathing.

You look at the signs.

The stations flash past too fast to read.

You ask someone what time the next stop is due.

He looks at his watch.

**"In exactly enough time not to be late."**

choices.text: Gently wake the man standing up
Stay on the train to see the next stop
Get off at the imaginary next stop

restaurant_express.title: Express Restaurant
restaurant_express.narrator: Here, the dishes arrive before the hunger does.
restaurant_express.text:
You walk into a tiny restaurant.

The waiter hands you the bill before you've even sat down.

The dishes are already on the table.
Already half eaten.
Already cold.

**"Fast service is our specialty."**

You ask whether you can order a blanquette.

He stares at you.

**"That takes three hours."**

As if it were an insult.

**"Exactly."**

choices.text: Open your bag and serve something real
Pay before you've eaten

table_ville.title: The Table of Slowing Down
table_ville.narrator: The first act of resistance is sometimes simply to set a tablecloth down.
table_ville.text:
You set a small table in the middle of the sidewalk.

It's absurd.

So of course, it draws a few glances.

You put a blanquette from a container on it.
Glasses.
Bread.

The passersby slow down.

One of them stops.

**"What's this?"**

**"A meal."**

**"How long does it take?"**

**"As long as it needs."**

He sits down.

choices.text: Move on with the shining ladle

fin_pas_le_temps.title: No Time
fin_pas_le_temps.narrator: From always arriving soon, you sometimes forget where you were going.
fin_pas_le_temps.text:
You start to run.

At first, it's to keep up with the others.
Then so as not to be in their way.
Then because everyone is running.

Your steps speed up.

The ladle falls somewhere behind you.

You don't stop to pick it up.

Your watch runs faster and faster.

The hands spin so fast they seem to stand still.

Somewhere, a shop is closing.

The neon sign goes out.

fin_retard.title: Late
fin_retard.narrator: Being late is a loop wearing brand-new shoes.
fin_retard.text:
You run with the student.

You turn left.

Then right.

Then left again.

The streets repeat themselves.

The screens repeat themselves.

The passersby repeat themselves.

After an impossible amount of time, you finally arrive.

In front of you:

the same avenue.

The same bench.

The same old lady.

The same student gathering his papers.

He looks at you.

**"I'm late."**

And you realize that you are, too.

fin_metro.title: The Last Stop
fin_metro.narrator: Some journeys only feel long because you never dare to get off.
fin_metro.text:
The subway keeps going.

The lights flicker.

The voice announces:

> Next stop:
> Your retirement.

Nobody moves.

The man standing up is still asleep.

His watch has shown the same time for two stations.

You look at yours.

It has stopped too.

Without your noticing.

hub_admin.title: The Second Door
hub_admin.narrator: The dream won't let you leave with just one good deed.
hub_admin.text:
You return behind your floating counter.

The shining ladle rests near the register.

The clock door has closed gently.

The city that was running is finally breathing.

But the other two doors are still there.

The morning door still doesn't appear.

The cat jumps onto the counter, nudges the salami with one paw, then stares at the door covered in forms.

On the notebook, a new sentence writes itself:

> You cannot wake up while the paperwork is still dreaming.

You understand.

The dream isn't over.

choices.text: Go through the administrative door with your bag

admin_intro.title: The Office of Forms
admin_intro.narrator: Here the corridors are straight, but no one ever reaches the end.
admin_intro.text:
You arrive in a gray building.

Mountains of files rise up to the ceiling.

Clocks everywhere.
All showing different times.
All wrong.

A man hands you a form.

**"What's it for?"**

**"To request the form for the reason of your visit."**

You look at the clocks.

They are moving.
But not in the right direction.

*I could fix them*, you think.

*That's not the question here*, you realize.

choices.text: Take a ticket
Look for the administrative elevator
Talk to the man with the paper clips
Organize a lunch break

ticket_admin.title: Ticket A38
ticket_admin.narrator: Waiting gets stranger when nobody knows why.
ticket_admin.text:
You take a ticket.

It reads:

> A38

The display board shows:

> A2

A woman has been waiting here for so long that she brought a plant.

The plant has taken a ticket of its own.

You look at the student.

He has been filling out the same line for several minutes.

Name:
Reason for the name:
Proof of the reason:

His hands are shaking.

The cat wanders between the chairs and falls asleep on ticket A3.

Nobody knows anymore whether the line can move at all.

choices.text: Take something out of your bag and share it
Wait your turn like everyone else

ascenseur_admin.title: The Administrative Elevator
ascenseur_admin.narrator: Even going up one floor sometimes requires a complete file.
ascenseur_admin.text:
The elevator is at the end of the corridor.

A metallic voice announces:

> Please provide proof of ascent.

You press the button.

The voice goes on:

> Please provide a certificate proving that you are allowed to press the button.

The cat sleeps in front of the buttons.

It purrs.

The elevator no longer dares to ask anything.

A faceless employee whispers:

**"It's been jamming the system since this morning. It's the calmest day we've had in years."**

choices.text: Enjoy the calm by organizing a lunch break
Look for the papers requested

trombones.title: The Paper Clip Man
trombones.narrator: Some tasks outlive the memory of their purpose.
trombones.text:
A man is sorting paper clips by color.

Red.
Blue.
Gray.
A grayer gray than the other gray.

You ask him whether it's urgent.

He looks at you with the eyes of someone who hasn't heard the word *urgent* in so long that he no longer knows what it means.

**"It's my job."**

**"And before?"**

He sorts one more paper clip.

**"I used to repair watches."**

choices.text: Tell him some things are meant to be shared, not sorted
Help him sort the paper clips

pause_dej.title: Gears, Bread and Stamps
pause_dej.narrator: An office becomes less dreadful when someone breaks bread in it.
pause_dej.text:
You set the bread and the salami on the counter.

A giant stamp stops in mid-air.

The employees look up.

When did they last eat something real?

One of them reaches for the bread.

Another hesitates.

As if taking time to eat were an unfiled form.

choices.text: Slip a useless stamp into your bag

admin_resolution.title: The Useless Stamp
admin_resolution.narrator: The best tools are sometimes the ones you decide to stop using.
admin_resolution.text:
You pick a small stamp up from the counter.

It bears a strange mark:

> PASSED — Approved as an exception

You stamp it onto your own form.

Nobody objects.

Perhaps because nobody knows exactly which stamps are official.

Or perhaps because you look like someone who knows what they're doing with small precision tools.

choices.text: Move on with the useless stamp

fin_formulaire.title: The Final Form
fin_formulaire.narrator: Some traps begin with a checkbox.
fin_formulaire.text:
You take the form.

It has only one page.

Then two.

Then twenty.

You are asked for your name, then the reason for your name, then a certificate proving you have a reason.

You sit down to fill it in more comfortably.

When you look up, you're behind a desk.

In front of you, someone is waiting.

You want to help them.

But a sentence leaves your mouth before you can stop it:

**"Your signature is missing."**

A stamp appears in your hand.

Again.

Again.

Again.

fin_employe.title: Employee of the Month
fin_employe.narrator: Some promotions look like traps with an ergonomic chair.
fin_employe.text:
You wait.

The display changes from A2 to A2 bis.

Then A2 complementary.

Then A2 final version.

After a while, an employee hands you a badge.

> EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH.

You try to explain that you don't work here.

He smiles at you.

**"That's what all the new ones say."**

Your desk appears.

Your chair appears.

Your onboarding form appears.

A note is stuck to it:

> Your lunch break is scheduled in 17 years.

hub_market.title: The Third Door
hub_market.narrator: One good thing often leads to another.
hub_market.text:
You return behind your floating counter.

The shining ladle rests near the register.
The useless stamp now serves as a paperweight.

Two doors have closed.

The hurried city is slowing down.
The administration is breathing.

But the neon of the third door is still flickering.

The cat jumps onto the counter.

It sniffs the air, looks at you, then looks at the neon door.

On the notebook, a sentence appears:

> Some people get lost by running.
> Others get lost by buying what they didn't need.

The morning door still isn't here.

There is one more world to cross.

choices.text: Go through the neon door with your bag

market_intro.title: The Endless Supermarket
market_intro.narrator: Here, everything is in stock. Except the way out.
market_intro.text:
You arrive in a huge supermarket.

The neon lights hum.

The aisles repeat endlessly in the mirrors.
The disposable watch section stretches for seven full aisles.

*Waterproof to 50 meters.*
*One-year warranty, non-renewable.*
*Accuracy: ±5 minutes per month.*

You look at one of them.

It's already 4 minutes behind.

It has only just come out of the box.

choices.text: Talk to the customer with the overflowing cart
Explore the canned goods aisle
Head to the self-checkout
Set up a table in the middle of the aisle

cliente_chariot.title: The Overflowing Cart
cliente_chariot.narrator: Some carts are full of things you never really wanted.
cliente_chariot.text:
The customer pushes an enormous cart.

It overflows with identical boxes.

You ask her what she's buying.

**"Time savings."**

She shows you the boxes.

*Saves 12 minutes a day.*
*More efficient.*
*Family size.*

**"And with that saved time, what do you do?"**

She stops.

She really thinks about it.

**"I'm looking for a way to save even more."**

choices.text: Share the chicken with the other customers
Follow the promotions with her

conserves.title: The Canned Goods Aisle
conserves.narrator: When everything is preserved, even hesitation lasts a long time.
conserves.text:
The old lady reads the ingredients on a can of peas.

She puts it back.

She picks up another one.

Puts it back.

**"Are you looking for something in particular?"**

**"I'm looking for peas that grew somewhere."**

She points to the label.

*Origin: Produced in an optimized zone.*

**"Before, I knew where what I ate came from."**

You understand.

It's what you feel about mass-produced watches.

choices.text: Open the can and serve it with the chicken
Compare every can one by one

caisses_auto.title: The Self-Checkouts
caisses_auto.narrator: Some machines are very good at saying no.
caisses_auto.text:
The self-checkout repeats:

> Unexpected item in bagging area.

You place an old pocket watch on the belt.

> Unexpected item in bagging area.

**"I know."**

You take it back.

The machine doesn't know what to do with an object that lasts.

choices.text: Unplug the register and invite the line to eat
Keep scanning until it understands

table_market.title: The Kitchen That Got Too Big
table_market.narrator: When people remember they're hungry, the aisles stop being endless.
table_market.text:
You set the roast chicken down on a small table.

Nobody knows where the table came from.

The customers come closer.
Some have forgotten that you can eat without a screen in front of you.

A child asks what it is.

**"A meal."**

**"How long does it take?"**

**"As long as it needs."**

He sits down on the floor.

It's a good start.

choices.text: Move on with the small neon light

fin_carte.title: Loyalty Card
fin_carte.narrator: Some rewards cost more than the purchases.
fin_carte.text:
You follow the promotions.

A loyalty card appears in your hand.

Then a second one.

Then a third.

Each card promises more benefits than the last.

A voice announces:

> Congratulations, you are now a priority customer.

The aisles open before you.

Your cart grows.

Your pockets fill with receipts.

You no longer know what you meant to buy.

But you've earned 3% on something.

Later, much later, you sleep in the bedding aisle.

The checkout wishes you good night.

fin_bug.title: Unexpected Item
fin_bug.narrator: The bug was perhaps the only thing still sincere.
fin_bug.text:
You keep scanning.

BEEP.

> Unexpected item in bagging area.

BEEP.

> Unexpected item in bagging area.

BEEP.

> Unexpected item in bagging area.

The world shakes.

The neon lights flicker.

The customers freeze.

The cat watches you.

It seems almost disappointed.

The checkout resumes:

> Unexpected customer in existence zone.

Then the whole world freezes.

fin_rayon_12.title: Aisle 12
fin_rayon_12.narrator: Every exit looks like a sale once you no longer know what you're looking for.
fin_rayon_12.text:
You compare the boxes.

Extra-fine peas.
Very fine peas.
Almost sincere peas.
Limited-edition peas.
Peas with a promise of happiness.

The aisles repeat themselves.

Your basket grows heavier.

You don't remember putting anything in it.

A jingle loops over the speakers.

**"Exceptional offer. Exceptional offer. Exceptional offer."**

You pass aisle 12.

Then again.

Then again.

After a while, you understand.

You're no longer looking for the exit.

You're only looking for the next aisle.

final_hub.title: The Calmed Counter
final_hub.narrator: The dream keeps the traces of whatever was warmed up in it.
final_hub.text:
You return behind your floating workbench.

This time, everything is different.

The watches on the shelves run at the right speed.
Not too fast.
Not too slow.

The blanquette is hot.

Outside, a few people have slowed down.
Not many.
Just enough to notice that the sky exists.

choices.text: Prepare the final banquet
Open the morning door
Watch the dream fade away gently

banquet.title: The Banquet of Ordinary Worlds
banquet.narrator: The coldest worlds sometimes mend themselves around a table that's too big.
banquet.text:
You serve the blanquette to the hurried people.

You repair a watch for the employees who are waiting.
You cut the salami for the people from the supermarket.
You offer bread to the old lady on the bench.

Nobody runs during this meal.

It isn't much.

Just a meal.
Just a few people sitting down.
Just a watchmaker who knows that some things cannot be hurried.

choices.text: Open the morning door
Let the dream come to an end

reveil.title: Morning Opens
reveil.narrator: Some doors open before you even touch the handle.
reveil.text:
You slowly open your eyes.

Morning light streams through the shop window.

For a few seconds,
you don't move.

You hear:

- The ticking of the hands.
- The sound of the city starting up again.
- The sound of your own breathing.

You get up.

You put a bottle of wine in the fridge for tonight.

The blanquette has been simmering since yesterday.

You open the shop.

*Horlogerie Verneuil — Repairs & Restorations*

The neon sign flickers once.

Then it lights up.
